thread.title: Austin lands $1B Apple campus, Portland outposts expected to grow

author: Will Anderson
title: Austin lands $1B Apple campus, Portland outposts expected to grow
text: – Portland Business Journal Dec 13, 2018, 11:23am PST Apple Inc. plans to build a $1 billion office campus in North Austin, not far from where it already has a major corporate hub. The company announced at 2 a.m. local time Dec. 13 that the new 133-acre facility will be able to handle about 5,000 employees when it opens, and could grow to house up to 15,000. Also included in the announcement were plans to grow other outposts, including those in Portland. Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) — which said it already employs about 6,200 people in Central Texas, the most outside the headquarters in Cupertino, Calif. — expects this move to make it the largest private employer in the Austin region. "Apple is proud to bring new investment, jobs and opportunity to cities across the United States and to significantly deepen our quarter-century partnership with the city and people of Austin," CEO Tim Cook said in a statement. "Talent, creativity and tomorrow’s breakthrough ideas aren’t limited by region or zip code, and, with this new expansion, we’re redoubling our commitment to cultivating the high-tech sector and workforce nationwide." Jobs at the new campus will include engineering, research and development, operations, finance, sales and customer support. Apple has several offices in Portland metro. Earlier this spring several job postings for roles in Washington County revealed the company has a small team working on hardware and related software. An Oregonian report noted the Cupertino company was hiring former Intel employees. The company has had an office in Vancouver for years. That downtown location has about 40 employees, according to a GeekWire report . That office develops productivity software for desktop and mobile applications like iWork and has historically worked closely with a team in Pittsburgh. According to Apple’s news release this morning, it intends to bolster the Portland office, though specifics on exact location weren’t offered. A spokesman said the company had no more details to offer regarding its hiring plans or how many non-retail workers the company employs in the Portland metro. In a news release this is all Apple had to say about Portland: “Apple plans to grow its employee base in regions across the United States over the next three years, expanding to over 1,000 employees in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City each, and adding hundreds of new jobs in Pittsburgh, New York, Boulder, Boston and Portland, Oregon.” In addition to retail stores and technical offices, Apple also has an expansive data center in Prineville in Central Oregon. As part of this overall expansion, the company said it will invest $10 billion in data centers in the next five years. All of the company’s data centers run on renewable energy. Apple was instrumental in the creation of Oregon’s largest solar power plant. Politicians gushed Apple's praise in the announcement. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott said it was "among the world’s most innovative companies," Mayor Steve Adler called it "a vital part of the Austin community for a quarter century" and Rebecca Clemons, Williamson County's director of administration, said it "is truly a part of our Texas family." Austin is already Apple's largest corporate hub outside its headquarters in Cupertino, Calif. When counting contractors, Apple has about 7,000 workers in the Texas capital, according to the Austin American-Statesman . Apple said it added 6,000 U.S. jobs in 2018 and now employs 90,000 people in all 50 states.
